references.text: The parallel account in Mark where Jesus sends the healed man home and tells him to report what the Lord has done for him, and the man proclaims it throughout the Decapolis.
The parallel account in Matthew about the demon-possessed men in the country of the Gadarenes, where Jesus heals them.
The psalmist urges us to come and hear, so that he may tell what God has done for his soul—the same theme as Jesus' command to report what God has done.
An invitation to thank the Lord for His mercy and proclaim His deeds with joy—to bear witness to what God has done.
The preceding context in Luke about the demon-possessed man in the country of the Gerasenes, which provides background for Jesus' command to go home and tell about God's deeds.
Isaiah urges us to make known among the nations the Lord's deeds and proclaim that His name is exalted—parallel to the mission to proclaim what God has done.
The healed leper began to preach and spread the word about what had happened, in a similar way to how the man in Luke 8:39 proclaims it throughout the city.
The Samaritan woman returned to the town and told the people about Jesus and what He had done—the same pattern of bearing witness to Jesus' deeds in her hometown.
The man born blind testifies about what Jesus has done for him, a personal testimony of God's power, just like the man in Luke 8:39.
